ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AC intersects BD at point E, with AD $\parallel$ BC. If $AE : AC = 1 : 3$, what is the ratio ${S}_{\triangle AED} : {S}_{\triangle CEB}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because AE: AC = 1: 3$,\\
$\therefore AE: EC = 1: 2$,\\
$\because AD \parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADE \sim \triangle CBE$,\\
$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle ADE}}{S_{\triangle CBE}} = \left(\frac{AE}{EC}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$

method.method_draft: Use triangle similarity. From the image, note that AC and BD cross at E, forming the right-side triangle AED and the left-side triangle CEB; AD and BC are the opposite side segments and are given parallel. From the text, use AE:AC = 1:3, so EC = AC - AE and AE:EC = 1:2. Because AD ∥ BC, angles DAE and ECB are corresponding/alternate interior angles, and angles AED and CEB are vertical angles, so triangles AED and CEB are similar. Their corresponding linear ratio is AE:EC = 1:2, so their area ratio is the square of the linear ratio: S_triangle AED : S_triangle CEB = 1^2:2^2 = 1:4.
